column1: The Taylor principle is an important policy lesson that has emerged from the new Keynesian model. It has been argued that the failure of central banks such as the Federal Reserve to respond su‰ciently strongly to inflation during the 1970s provides an explanation for the rise in inflation experiences at the time (Lubik and Schorfheide 2004). Further, Orphanides (2001) argued that estimated Taylor rules for the Federal Reserve are sensitive to whether real-time data are used, and he found a much weaker response to inflation in the 1987–1999 period based on real-time data.
